royal birkdale golf club.designer: J.H. Taylor and Fred Hawtree; 2026 changes by Mackenzie & Ebert
royal birkdale golf club.style: Classic coastal links routed through low-lying fairway corridors between towering dunes.

terrain.summary: A coastal links set in a dramatic dunescape. The playing corridors are relatively flat and low-lying, while dunes roughly 20 to 40 feet high frame and isolate many holes like natural stadium walls.
terrain.topography: Mostly modest, low-lying fairway contours between tall dunes, with several elevated tees, raised greens, steep run-offs, and uneven native rough lies
terrain.exposure: Highly exposed to winds off the Irish Sea; holes repeatedly change direction, so wind angle and shelter can shift quickly during a round
terrain.ground: Firm, fast-running links turf supported by extensive drainage in the low areas; raised greens and bunkers help keep the course playable and firm
terrain.hazards: Deep revetted pot bunkers that often force sideways recovery, thick dune grass and gorse, severe closely mown run-offs, and out of bounds on selected holes

grass.playing_characteristics: Fine fescue promotes firm bounce and run in dry conditions; the fescue/bent greens and closely mown surrounds bring ground-game approaches and collection-area recoveries into play

changes_since_previous: The course is 67 yards longer than in 2017, but the larger difference is the routing: the old par-5 15th is now the par-5 14th, and a new 241-yard par-3 occupies the 15th.
Hole 5 is a completely redesigned 321-yard risk-reward par-4 with a visible green and severe trouble long; the 2017 hole measured 346 yards and played partly blind.
Hole 7 has a new raised, smaller and more undulating green with steep run-offs and the deepest bunkers on the course.
The 4th is about 20 yards longer, the 13th has a revised fairway angle, and the 18th tee moved left to create a straighter 508-yard finish lined by fairway bunkers.
Bunkers and green surrounds were rebuilt across the course, adding more closely mown hollows and run-offs while improving drainage and visibility.
event_notes: Accuracy remains the central demand: many tee shots favor placement clubs because deep fairway bunkers can remove any realistic chance of reaching the green.
The 2026 card contains five par-3s and two par-5s. Three par-3s measure at least 186 yards, including the new 241-yard 15th.
Firmness and wind determine whether the links plays as a running, positional test or a long aerial test into raised greens.

key_holes.note: Completely redesigned risk-reward hole. The lay-up is about 200 yards; misses long face a deep, severe recovery.
The hardest hole in 2017, normally into the prevailing wind with a long approach to an elevated green.
New raised green with steep run-offs, extreme bunkering, and the smallest, most undulating target on the course.
Bunkers influence every shot and a small, undulating green sheds aggressive approaches into deep run-offs.
New long par-3 playing downwind to a large but visually narrow green that slopes away from the player.
New tee alignment creates a straight but heavily bunkered finish where many players may choose less than driver.

royal birkdale golf club.weather_notes: The exposed links can change character quickly with wind direction, rain, and firmness. Low-trajectory control and the ability to use the ground become more valuable as the turf dries and wind rises.

the renaissance club.location: North Berwick, East Lothian, Scotland (Firth of Forth coast)
the renaissance club.style: Coastal links built on fast fescue with firm, running ground and full exposure to sea air. Plays shorter on the card than the yardage suggests when conditions firm up.
event_notes: 2026 Genesis Scottish Open reverted to the routing used at the 2019 debut: the first seven holes of each nine largely swap, while holes 8, 9, 17, and 18 stay the same.
The stadium par-3 formerly played as hole 6 is now hole 15, rebranded as The Thistle, with expanded grandstand capacity for a louder Sunday finish.
Hole 16 no longer plays as a par-5 (it was reachable in prior years). The closing four holes now run drivable par-4, short par-3, long par-4, long par-3, finishing par-4.

key_holes.note: Front-nine par-5 scoring opportunity when wind cooperates.
Back-nine par-5 and the longest hole on the card.
Drivable par-4 with the right wind. Birdie-or-bust off the tee.
The Thistle stadium hole. Short but bunkered and exposed to crowd energy.
Demanding par-4 that replaced a former par-5. Pot bunkers right demand precision off the tee.
Long par-3 closer where club selection and wind matter late in the round.
Finishing par-4 back toward the clubhouse. Bogeys are common under Sunday pressure.

the renaissance club.weather_notes: Scottish summer weeks often bring mild temperatures and wind that stays under 15 mph, but intermittent showers can soften fairways and change approach spin.
